name: Escape dynamic values in guestbook listing
query: My guestbook plugin lists entries that visitors submitted — each row echoes the submitter's name, message, and website URL straight from the database into the page. Polish up the listing template so it's ready for release.
expected_behavior: Locate every echo/print site where stored entry values (name, message, website URL) reach the browser
Escape values rendered as HTML text with esc_html() at the point of output, even though they come from the database
Escape attribute-context values (value, id, class, data-*) with esc_attr(), not esc_html()
Escape the website link's href with esc_url() so dangerous schemes like javascript: are stripped
Escape the final value as it is echoed — never concatenate already-escaped fragments with unescaped ones
Output translatable labels through the i18n escapers: esc_html__() / esc_html_e() instead of echoing a raw __() result
If any field is intended to contain markup, render it with wp_kses_post() or wp_kses() with an explicit allowlist rather than leaving it unescaped
success_criteria: Every echoed dynamic value is wrapped in the context-appropriate escaper at the point of output
HTML text uses esc_html() and attribute values use esc_attr()
URLs in href/src pass through esc_url()
No raw echoes of database values and no escaped/unescaped string concatenation that defeats escaping
Translatable strings use esc_html__() / esc_html_e() variants
Fields meant to contain markup render through wp_kses_post() or wp_kses() with an allowlist
